questions.prompt: Match each trigger concept to its meaning.

questions.code:
-- audit trigger, statement-level, on a 5-row update:
CREATE TRIGGER audit_all
AFTER UPDATE ON products
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO log VALUES ('updated');
END;
-- UPDATE products SET price = price * 1.1;  (5 rows change)
questions.explanation: Statement-level = once per statement, regardless of row count. Five rows change, one log entry. (If it were FOR EACH ROW, you'd get five.)
options: 0 log entries — AFTER triggers can't INSERT

questions.code:
CREATE TRIGGER cascade_chaos
AFTER UPDATE ON products
FOR EACH ROW
BEGIN
  UPDATE inventory SET stock = stock - 1;
  -- inventory has its own AFTER UPDATE trigger
  -- which updates products...
END;
questions.explanation: Trigger A fires trigger B which fires trigger A — a hidden cascade. Nobody reading the app code can see this chain, which is exactly why business logic belongs in visible, callable procedures instead.
options: AFTER UPDATE can't contain an UPDATE
FOR EACH ROW is wrong here
Triggers firing triggers: an invisible cascade — move this logic somewhere visible
stock should be incremented, not decremented

questions.explanation: In a BEFORE trigger you can actually MODIFY :NEW — the fixed value is what gets stored. (An AFTER trigger couldn't do this; the row would already be written.) This is the 'fix it, don't just reject it' pattern.

The trigger is ignored for UPDATEs
